items.title: Sheryl Bailey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 24, 2023
items.q: he’s a big influence on me as a guitarist but as a composer.

ctx.x: That’s all right. I’d rather glad that it doesn’t have a particular name because I’m sure I wouldn’t know what it is.

No. Well, and it starts on — no it’s not true, anyway it’s just a melody but yes, that’s kind of an interesting tune. People like that tune a lot. And I wrote it and then I realized later, much time later, you know part of this celebration for Pat Martino was an amazing event, but anyway you know there’s a lot of discussion about, you know, and he’s a big influence on me as a guitarist but as a composer. But there was a whole thing about an exercise that he had with minor seven chords that moved down in whole…

The tune at some point after the walking up melodies, the scales, switched into something else. And I had this feeling like — not to try and get inside your head — but you felt it was time for something else. Like okay here’s the bridge. It’s something different. How do those things occur to you?
